title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: Adds wireless Android device connection and pairing via mDNS, and reduces annotation scan CPU overhead with incremental processing.

highlights.title: WiFi Android Connection
highlights.description: Connect to Android devices over WiFi using automatic mDNS discovery — no USB cable required after initial setup.

highlights.title: Guided ADB WiFi Pairing
highlights.description: A new step-by-step pairing flow walks through first-time wireless setup, making it accessible without prior adb experience.

highlights.title: Incremental Annotation Scanning
highlights.description: Hex color and null-assertion providers now reprocess only changed lines on each edit, cutting CPU overhead in annotation-heavy files.

sections.heading: Improvements
bullets: Added a Connect via ADB WiFi command that uses mDNS (dns-sd) to discover Android devices on the local network and connects wirelessly — removes the need for a USB cable after first setup.
Added a Pair via ADB WiFi flow with guided step-by-step instructions for first-time wireless pairing.
HexColorFoldingProvider and NullAssertionProvider now perform incremental line scanning — only lines that changed are reprocessed on each edit, reducing CPU overhead in files with many annotations.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Fixed a race condition where ADB WiFi connection failed because IP resolution had not yet completed — the extension now connects using the stable .local mDNS hostname.
Fixed device detection to prefer the HOST:PORT address format and fall back to the adb-XXXX-YYYY serial, preventing misidentified or dropped device connections.
